text: The Patriots' dominant 45-17 demolition of the Raiders on Sunday represented Drake Maye's best performance of the season, as the young quarterback accounted for five total touchdowns despite operating without his top receiver and facing a defense that was already undermanned with both starting cornerbacks sidelined—a performance that suggests Maye has finally found his confidence and his deep ball after an rocky start to the year. The victory came at a cost, however, as RB TreVeyon Henderson suffered an ankle injury and LT Will Campbell exited with what sources told NFL Network is believed to be a knee sprain, adding to New England's mounting injury concerns heading into the week. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's resilience in his Monday press conference, and film review confirms that both Maye's individual play and the defense's execution were standout performances in what became a dominant Week 5 showcase at Gillette Stadium, all while the Patriots wore throwback uniforms as part of the league's uniform rotation.
